Then per class: distinct tickets, first_seen_at gaps and days (scratch/resume-census10/an.py, an2.py, an3.py). verdicts.note: The counts are exact: khala has github-permissions 71, workflow-permissions 69, github-write-access 69 and codex-usage-limit 41; aiur has github-broker-unavailable 61 and paused-before_run_failure 65. The four khala slug strings do not occur in aiur. But the conclusion does not follow. (1) The wakes are re-asks, not repeat failures. DecisionAttention re-asks an open attention every 15 min, and the gaps between wakes are exactly 15 min. github-permissions: 70 wakes on one ticket and 1 on a second. workflow-permissions: 69 wakes, 1 ticket. github-write-access: 69 wakes, 1 ticket. All three ran 09-16 19:30 to 09-17 12:46, about 17 h. codex-usage-limit: 41 wakes, 1 ticket, 09-25 12:06-22:06. (2) The three khala permission classes are one incident. The Executor handoff and history say that tickets 10, 11 and 50 were paused for the same reason: the agent bot account had only read permission on the new khala repo. Three agents gave the same cause three different slugs, and the slugs are free text. (3) aiur had the same kind of storm under other names. On 08-21 there were github-broker-unavailable 61 (6 tickets; 50 wakes are re-asks on 2 tickets), github-broker 36, github-budget-broker 28, credentials 26, push-identity 25, auth-identity 25 and github-identity 12, all on that one day. This matches the credential-pool and identity-split changes merged that day. (4) Time window: the aiur stream ends 09-20, so it could not record the 09-25 usage limit. aiur did record usage-limit pauses (6 paused-usage_limit_exhausted on 08-22), and khala had 31 of them, one per ticket, on 09-25/26. (5) Only paused-before_run_failure repeats across many tickets: 65 wakes, 46 tickets, 62 separate episodes per ticket, but 57 of the 65 fall on 08-21..24. Inflation overall: aiur has 783 attention wakes but 334 distinct (ticket, slug) pairs; khala has 513 but 130. For load_bearing: most of this repetition comes from re-asks and wake dedup, not from repeated dispatch or credential failures. The permission gap was real but happened once per repo.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The ticket.agent.attention counts are exact (khala: github-permissions 71, workflow-permissions 69, github-write-access 69, codex-usage-limit 41; aiur: github-broker-unavailable 61, paused-before_run_failure 65), but most are 15-minute DecisionAttention re-asks of one open attention, not repeat failures. Each khala class is one ticket (github-permissions: 70 + 1 on a second ticket). The three khala permission slugs are one incident: on 2026-09-16/17 the bot account had read-only access to the newly onboarded khala repo, and three agents named it three ways. The 41 codex-usage-limit wakes are one ticket over 10 h on 09-25. aiur's 61 github-broker-unavailable wakes are one 08-21 outage across 6 tickets (50 re-asks on 2 tickets). They are part of a same-day GitHub broker/credential/identity cluster of about 213 wakes under 7 slugs. The slugs are free text chosen by agents, and the windows do not overlap for the usage limit (the aiur stream ends 09-20; aiur logged 6 usage-limit pauses on 08-22). So the repos differ mostly in naming and timing, not in failure type. Each repo had one GitHub-credential attention storm. The one genuinely multi-ticket recurrent class is aiur paused-before_run_failure (46 tickets, 57 of 65 wakes on 08-21..24). Attention wakes overstate distinct incidents: 783 vs 334 distinct (ticket, slug) pairs in aiur, 513 vs 130 in khala.
